title: USS Chemicals Neville Island Plant: “Proud of Our Progress”
caption: Full-page advertisement tracing the plant's lineage in its own words: Davison Coke & Iron formed in 1928, Pittsburgh Coke & Chemical “created” in 1944, and the Pittsburgh Chemical Company a division of U.S. Steel from 1964. Other records date the PC&C name to about 1942 and the USS Chemicals Division to 1966. Page 59 of an unidentified Coraopolis-area community booklet.
credit: Unidentified booklet, p. 59; via the Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley Railway Tumblr

title: “Steel Mill to Be Erected” (1899)
caption: American Steel and Wire announces a $1,000,000 plant on Neville Island, opposite its two Woods Run blast furnaces in Allegheny, to be joined to them by a bridge over the Ohio. The plans called for Bessemer, blooming, rolling, rod and wire mills and docks for river coal. What was built instead was a single blast furnace and the P&OV.
credit: The New York Times, 27 October 1899; clipping posted by Mark Connolly on the Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley Railway Tumblr

title: Pittsburgh, Chartiers & Youghiogheny Railway, by Ivan W. Saunders
caption: First page of a short PC&Y history: chartered 26 October 1881, built McKees Rocks–Beechmont 1882–83, and joined to the Neville Island Branch over the back-channel bridge, the only rail entrance to the island it shared with the P&OV.

rights: Journal article; check JSTOR terms before reuse.

title: P&OV Locomotive 4 at the Monongahela Railway shop
caption: Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley Railway No. 4 at the Monongahela Railway locomotive repair shop, June 1994. The University of Pittsburgh record calls it the “Monongahela Railroad” shop; the Monongahela Railway had been taken into Conrail in 1993, and the record does not say where the shop was. In earlier years P&OV heavy repairs were done at the P&LE shops in McKees Rocks. The P&OV served the steel and coke plants on Neville Island and shut down in 1994.
credit: Ken Kobus. Ken Kobus Photograph Collection, AIS.2006.18, Archives & Special Collections, University of Pittsburgh Library System
rights: In Copyright (rights statement on the ULS record).
